fields.title: Labor markets and occupational work
modules: LM-01
Youth employment, unemployment and NEET measurement
Joblessness, informal work, underemployment and participation require different measures.
LM-02
Occupational injuries, exposure and underreporting
Injury rates, hazard exposure, employer reporting and regulatory coverage are distinct.

fields.title: Transport safety and mobility
modules: TR-01
Road traffic mortality and preventable injury
Deaths, exposure, enforcement, roads, vehicles and emergency response are distinct mechanisms.
TR-02
Safe access for pedestrians, cyclists and other vulnerable road users
Street safety, transport access, exposure, design and injury risk differ across user groups.

fields.title: Air quality and environmental exposure
modules: AQ-01
Ambient air pollution exposure and health burden
PM2.5, spatial exposure, monitoring completeness and attributable health burden must be distinguished.
AQ-02
Air-quality standards, measurement and comparability
Guidelines, measurement stations, settlement means and pollutant indicators are not interchangeable.

fields.title: Disaster risk and preparedness
modules: DR-01
Multi-hazard early warning coverage and last-mile reach
Declared warning systems, forecast skill, communications, comprehension and protective action are different requirements.
DR-02
Disaster loss measurement and cascading economic impacts
Direct damages, disruption, ecosystem effects and reported losses require separate measures.

new_module_origin: Breadth diversification, independently selected from previous nine fields; not from original 54-node Deep Research CSV

bridges.boundary: Foundational skills can inform workforce preparation but labor-market outcomes and schooling outcomes are distinct.
Income and labor markets are relevant household-resource context; no quantification of housing affordability here.
Workplace and ambient air hazards can overlap; exposure populations and methods differ.
Injury burden may involve emergency/health service capacity; no locality-specific link observed.
Transport modes and urban environmental exposure coexist but no reduction effect is verified.
Transport location/access may affect residential accessibility; not proven housing burden causality.
Air quality is a health risk context relevant to chronic disease; does not prove a specific intervention.
Housing exposure and ambient pollution may share contextual risk; measurements and scales differ.
Hydrological monitoring can inform warning systems but local warning effectiveness is unmeasured.
Warning dissemination requires communication pathways; telecom coverage is not confirmed delivery.
Housing climate exposure is one component of disaster risk; accounting dimensions differ.
Smallholder logistical infrastructure may involve connectivity; no site-level intervention evaluated.
Smart utility operations can depend on communications; not every water-balance tool uses connectivity.
Efficiency could alter electricity load; relationship has no location-specific grid evaluation.
Diet risk is relevant to NCD policy; no inferred diet-outcome effect.
Rabies control involves public-health service pathways, with no local care-capacity evaluation.
Educational data systems and privacy technology may intersect but this corpus lacks deployment proof.
Local data-centre load and water supply may interact; no individual site resource conflict shown.
Workplace emergency preparedness and public early warnings may interact; separate requirements.
